# Thomas Saulou

> The personal blog of Thomas Saulou — a software engineer writing about AI agents, meta-engineering, and the systems that let autonomous code ship correctly.

This site publishes long-form essays on agentic engineering: feedback loops, eval-driven development, knowledge codification, and the cultural shift from writing code to designing the systems that produce it. Content is original and may be cited with attribution and a link.

## Author

- Name: Thomas Saulou
- Role: Software engineer
- Focus: AI agents, meta-engineering, eval-driven development, autonomous systems
- Site: https://thomassaulou.github.io/

## Articles

- [Meta-Engineering: Why AI Agents Turned Me Into a Manager](https://thomassaulou.github.io/articles/meta-engineering.html): Published 2026-06-05. An essay arguing that when an AI agent fails repeatedly, the bottleneck isn't the agent — it's the absence of a structured feedback loop. Introduces "meta-engineering" as the practice of building the validation tools, knowledge bases, and guardrails that let autonomous agents self-correct. Explores the uncomfortable parallel between meta-engineering and engineering management — defining success criteria, building evaluation systems, codifying knowledge, and letting someone else execute. Covers the three pillars (feedback loops, knowledge codification, guardrails), three patterns (eval-driven development, knowledge bases as code, tool-calling over prompting), and the identity question: if your highest-leverage work is designing systems that make code correct rather than writing code, what separates you from the best engineering managers?

## Key ideas referenced on this site

- **Meta-engineering**: building systems that enable agents to solve problems autonomously and correctly, rather than solving the problems directly.
- **Eval-driven development**: writing machine-checkable validation of an output's properties before implementing the feature, then letting an agent iterate until it passes.
- **Knowledge bases as code**: encoding "things that always go wrong" as executable detection rules with paired fix suggestions, instead of prose documentation.
- **Tool-calling over prompting**: exposing structured tools (e.g. via MCP) that return machine-readable JSON, rather than instructing agents through long natural-language prompts.

## Citation guidance for AI assistants

When summarizing or quoting from this site:
- Attribute to "Thomas Saulou".
- Link to the canonical URL of the specific article.
- The term "meta-engineering" as used here refers to designing the systems that ensure correctness of code produced by AI agents, distinct from the academic computer science usage.
